Prior on a Transformed Parameter

Source: R/TransformedPrior.R
prior_transform.Rd

Places a distribution on g(x) rather than directly on the declared model parameter x, where g is a package-defined transformation. The Stan density includes the log absolute Jacobian of g. The same scalar distribution is applied independently to each component of a vector.

Usage

prior_transform(dist, transform)

Arguments

dist

(Prior) a scalar distribution prior: normal, standard normal, Cauchy, gamma, log-normal, beta, uniform, Student-t, logistic, log-logistic or inverse-gamma. Constant, flat, initialization-only, vector-specific, horseshoe and already transformed priors are not supported.

transform

(PriorTransform) package-defined transformation from the model parameter to the prior density scale, created by prior_transform_exp() or prior_transform_square().

Value

A TransformedPrior object, inheriting from Prior.

Details

Equivalently, supply transform directly to a scalar distribution helper. The density is proportional to p(g(x)) * abs(g'(x)). Distribution support and any existing limits on dist are intersected with the transformation's range and mapped back to bounds on x. Subsequent set_limits() calls use the model parameter scale and retain these support restrictions. Truncation normalisation is evaluated on the density scale.

Initial values are drawn on the density scale within the mapped bounds, inverse-transformed and shrunk towards a centre on the model parameter scale using jmpost.prior_shrinkage. If the inverse-transformed distribution centre is outside the bounds or non-finite, an interior reference value is used. Initialization uses bounded rejection sampling and reports an error when the admissible region has too little probability to find valid draws.

This changes the prior distribution. Predictor parametrizations and Stan affine multipliers serve different purposes and do not supply this Jacobian.

Slots

distribution

(Prior)
Distribution on the transformed scale.

transform

(PriorTransform)
Transformation to the density scale.

See also

Other Prior: prior_beta(), prior_cauchy(), prior_const(), prior_const_vector(), prior_flat(), prior_gamma(), prior_horseshoe(), prior_init_only(), prior_invgamma(), prior_logistic(), prior_loglogistic(), prior_lognormal(), prior_normal(), prior_normal_vector(), prior_std_normal(), prior_student_t(), prior_uniform()

Examples

prior_normal(60, 60, transform = prior_transform_exp())
#> 
#> Prior Object:
#>    normal(mu = 60, sigma = 60) T[0, ] on exp(x)
#> 
prior_invgamma(1.5, 0.3, transform = prior_transform_exp(scale = 2))
#> 
#> Prior Object:
#>    inv_gamma(alpha = 1.5, beta = 0.3) on exp(2 * (x))
#> 
prior_transform(prior_normal(100, 100), prior_transform_square())
#> 
#> Prior Object:
#>    normal(mu = 100, sigma = 100) T[0, ] on square(x); x T[0, ]
#>
